title: bronze_wgi's DQ row-count band (50-500,000) is too wide to catch a lost indicator
description:
bronze_wgi's row-count DQ check uses a (50, 500000) band against a normal load of ~31,000 rows across 6 governance indicators (~5,000 rows each). That band is wide enough that losing an entire indicator's worth of rows — the exact failure mode task-066 found and closed with an ingest-side completeness guard (all-6-indicators check before the overwrite) — would sail through this check undetected, dropping to ~26,000 rows and still landing well inside 50-500,000.

task-066's fix already prevents the silent write at the source (the notebook now raises before overwriting bronze_wgi if any indicator is missing), so this is defense-in-depth rather than closing an active hole. But the DQ check's stated purpose is to catch exactly this class of defect, and right now it structurally cannot for this table.

Re-derive an appropriate band from the real per-indicator row counts (measure live, don't guess) rather than picking a round number.
acceptanceCriteria: The real per-indicator and total row counts for bronze_wgi are measured from a live run, not assumed.
A tightened row-count band (or an indicator-count check, or both) is proposed and implemented such that losing one of the six indicators would actually fail the DQ check.

The new band/check is demonstrated NOT to false-positive against normal run-to-run variation (WGI is annual data, so row counts should be nearly static between runs — verify this assumption against real history rather than asserting it).
docs/data_quality_framework.md is updated to reflect the new band/check and why the old one was insufficient.
Erik's half: deploy and confirm the tightened check still passes on a normal run.
notes:
Created by the orchestrator from task-066's issues_discovered array (2026-08-13). Not yet reviewed by Erik under the out-of-spec gate — out_of_spec_approved is false. ---

[IMPLEMENTATION 2026-08-18] Band tightened from (50, 500000) to (28000, 45000), derived from live measurement.

AC1 (measured, not assumed): fetched all 6 WGI indicators from the World Bank API for 1996-2023 applying the SAME non-null filter the producer applies (fetch_indicator skips entries whose value is None). Per-indicator: CC.EST 5,158 | GE.EST 5,127 | PV.EST 5,214 | RL.EST 5,261 | RQ.EST 5,128 | VA.EST 5,234. Total 31,122. The API declared 5,400 entries per indicator and all 6 walked completely (entries_seen == declared on every one), so the non-null counts are exact, not truncated reads.

AC2 (losing an indicator now fails): worst case whole-indicator loss is 31,122 - 5,127 (smallest indicator) = 25,995 rows, which is below the new 28,000 floor and therefore FAILS. Under the old (50, 500000) it passed. The floor clears the worst case by ~2,000 rows so a substantially partial loss also trips. Ceiling 45,000 replaces the meaningless 500,000: it still fails a duplicate/fan-out write (2x = 62,244; 1.5x = 46,683) while leaving ~a decade of headroom at ~1,250 rows per added vintage (~208 countries x 6 indicators).

AC3 (no false positive, verified against real history rather than asserted): total was 31,122 on 2026-08-13 (task-066, measured through this project's own fetch_indicator during its pipeline run) and 31,122 again on 2026-08-18, with VA.EST at 5,234 in both — two independent measurements five days apart, identical. Structural reason for the invariance: WGI is an annual vintage AND p_start_year/p_end_year are hardcoded in bronze_ingest_wgi (task-072), so the window cannot widen without a code edit. HONEST LIMITATION, recorded rather than papered over: gold_quality_history persists only each check's SCORE, not total_rows (log_check_result accepts total_rows but the history writer projects only score/threshold/breach_flag/status), so a longer row-count history is NOT recoverable from the warehouse. The two measurements are the whole evidence base; I did not claim more.

AC4 (doc updated): docs/data_quality_framework.md § 2.1 gains a "Choosing a band: bronze_wgi (worked example)" subsection with the per-indicator table, both bound derivations, why (50, 500000) was insufficient, and the persistence limitation above.

AC5 is Erik's half: deploy and confirm the tightened check still passes on a normal run (expected 31,122, comfortably inside 28,000-45,000).

SCOPE NOTE: AC2 allows a band, an indicator-count check, or both. I implemented the band only. An explicit distinct-indicator-count check at the DQ layer would be strictly stronger, but it would mean touching the check registry and potentially BLOCKING_CHECKS — i.e. changing pipeline gate behaviour, which is a decision for Erik rather than an implicit scope expansion. Flagged as available in both the notebook comment and the doc.

NOT committed, NOT pushed — working-tree only.

[AC5 CONFIRMED 2026-08-19 — Erik's half closed, with an explicit caveat on what the evidence does and does not prove] Deployed via commit a862f42 (Deploy Fabric Artifacts run 32246904194, success) and exercised by orchestrator run 0f779394 (11:21:13->11:43:00Z, Completed).

MEASURED RESULT: dq_row_count_validation on oem_lh.bronze_wgi reads score 100.0, status 'pass', breach_flag false at 2026-08-19T11:38:16.93.

WHAT THAT DOES NOT PROVE, stated plainly: the check ALSO returned 100.0/pass before this change, because the old (50, 500000) band was wide enough to pass as well. The score alone therefore does not distinguish the new band from the old, and citing it by itself would be weak evidence.

WHAT ESTABLISHES IT: getDefinition against the live workspace BEFORE the run confirmed both directions — the deployed data_quality_checks carries ('oem_lh.bronze_wgi', 28000, 45000) and no longer carries ('oem_lh.bronze_wgi', 50, 500000). The pass is therefore a pass against the TIGHTENED band, which means the live row count lies inside 28,000-45,000. The count itself is not readable from gold_quality_history because total_rows is dropped at the persistence boundary — the exact limitation this task documented in docs/data_quality_framework.md § 2.1. An independent World Bank API walk on 2026-08-19 returned 31,122 with complete pagination on all six indicators, which is the source the table is built from 1:1, but that is a measurement of the SOURCE, not a read of the Delta table.
